title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement databases and camera systems is accused of querying them for personal reasons over a two month period. The systems worked as designed and returned the data they were built to return. The failure sits at the access and audit layer, where a privileged user's searches were not constrained to case-related purposes.

The controls that would catch this are purpose limitation and review of queries against a legitimate investigative need, plus alerting on searches that touch a person connected to the officer rather than to a case. The reporting does not say which of these existed at Coffee County or whether any alert fired. It also does not say whether the license plate data was retained or shared beyond the queries described.

The charges are allegations from a grand jury indictment, and an indictment is not a conviction. Nothing in the reporting establishes guilt, and nothing establishes what the department's oversight of database queries looked like before the GBI investigation began.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused law enforcement databases and camera systems for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the GBI investigation began.

The woman he is accused of tracking spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
